art.idea: The book opens at the threshold. The page is the Entry Court arch itself. The reader stands with the crew under the arch, looking into a long dark lane where one hand lamp makes the only warm circle. The arch is the page shape, the title is set over it like the gateway's lintel inscription, and the whole sheet is the darkest page of the chapter. Everything after this gets lighter.

art.idea: The knock comes from below, so the page is a shaft. A full-height narrow panel on the right drops the reader's eye down the lift shaft to the helper. The field darkens from aubergine at the top to warm store-timber at the foot, because the only new light is down there. The border is the brass safety gate: its rail runs down the left edge, and the lower-store timber landing is the page's floor.
art.role_in_opener: 3/5: the light moves. The page's warmth is at the bottom, pulling the eye down.
art.system: Book system (identical on every page, do not vary): V09 type (captions Source Serif 4 Regular 14/18 on caption paper #F7F1E3, .6pt brass #b3722f border, 5pt/8pt padding, soft shadow; speech Source Sans 3 Semibold 14/18 in ivory #FFFDF6 balloons, .8pt ink #1d2433 outline, curved P107-style tails ending short of the mouth; no speaker names). Panel frames 1pt brass + .5pt inner dark line + drop shadow, gutters 10pt, trim clearance 24pt. Border built in one full-sheet SVG like P107: rules 0.5–1.1pt, a pinstripe 12pt inside the trim broken at entry, folio and finish; strongest accent at entry (top-left) and finish (bottom-right). Moonclock folio bottom centre exactly as P107: brass ring r8 at (422,636), waxing moon lit fraction = page/107 (lit on the right), number Source Sans 3 Semibold 11pt at left:433pt top:629.5pt.

text: Why is −12°C colder than 12°C? We’ll start with numbers below zero, then explore equal groups, quick division checks, squares and cubes. Each idea will help you choose a calculation and understand why it works.

We’ll work through this chapter together. Keep a pencil nearby: when you reach a Try or Practice question, cover the working underneath and have a go. Then uncover it and compare the steps, not only the final number.

teaching.heading: Numbers below zero
questions: Sam’s town is at 12°C. Sarah’s town is at −12°C. Both temperatures contain 12, but Sarah will certainly want the warmer coat! What difference does that little minus sign make?
Pause and think. Why might Sam feel comfortable while Sarah feels very cold? If Sarah’s temperature rises by 10°C, will her town be as warm as Sam’s?
text: 12°C is 12 degrees above zero; −12°C is 12 degrees below zero. Sam’s town is warmer. From −12°C, a rise of 10°C takes Sarah’s town to −2°C:
−2°C is still colder than Sam’s 12°C. Sarah’s town has warmed up, but it has not caught up with Sam’s.

teaching.heading: Example 11
questions: Salim wants to pack 171 pencils, 27 erasers and 63 pens into gift packs. Every pack must contain the same number of pencils, the same number of erasers and the same number of pens, with nothing left over. Find the greatest number of packs and the number of each item in one pack.
text: Each kind of item must be shared equally, with none left over. So the number of packs must divide 171, 27 and 63 exactly. We want as many packs as possible: that means finding their HCF.
The common factors are 1, 3 and 9. The greatest is 9, so Salim can make 9 packs. Now share each kind of item among those 9 packs:
Each pack contains 19 pencils, 3 erasers and 7 pens. Every pack has that same mixture; the numbers 19, 3 and 7 do not have to match each other. Check the pencils, for example: 9 × 19 = 171.

pages.notes:
Chapter 01 finale (last story page). Show only the threshold reveal and the existing obstruction: no recipe correction, no drink calculation, no Chapter 02 action (nobody clears the cart or touches the serving controls). No human cooks; the Gate crowd is not shown. Evidence custody changes from Ahana to Tara only in P107-3. Tez's faded stripes persist. Speaker names, production notes and 'she says' never print. No lettering in any image.
design (V09): reader goal = feel the reveal, then the hand-over of responsibility. Hardest fit = P107-1's caption (5 sentences) and P107-5's two-sentence balloon. Chosen: hero reveal panel with a one-sided arch (threshold/reveal → manual p14 'arch entering from one side') beside Tez's tall reaction panel; below, a 3-beat strip from one camera (handover → 'Come.' → the boundary) whose narrow middle panel speeds the beat and whose wide last panel lets the chapter's last line land. Challenger rejected: 5 equal panels (loses the reveal's scale). Gutter: peacock teal #245857 (change of place: Food Street's teal canopies). Edge motif: Food Street canopy seam + brass post bracket (manual p15 'Canopy seam' + 'Lantern bracket'); entry accent top-left, finish bottom-right with a small hanging brass lantern.
